articles.title: Orchid Shift Pearl
articles.summary: The paint construction uses two interference-colour domain populations, seams and platelet accents. Its spec follows the domain light field and platelet coverage with varying metal and roughness; clearcoat starts at 16. Own palette runs in finish-colour mode; Use source paint skips primary paint generation.
articles.what: The paint construction uses two interference-colour domain populations, seams and platelet accents. Its spec follows the domain light field and platelet coverage with varying metal and roughness; clearcoat starts at 16. This is one of the five colour-bearing Foundation exceptions, not a plain source-passing material. Registered M/R/CC seed values are not uniform output values or a tested recommendation for your car. Source inspection describes construction; final appearance and any angle-dependent claim require actual in-sim inspection. In the reviewed ordinary primary-base compositor, BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only) skips the primary base paint function, including a colour-generating one. Use finish’s own color allows that palette to run. This preserves the source from the primary base paint pass, not from every other operation: patterns, additional bases, hue/saturation/brightness, explicit colour overrides and target/mask choices need separate checks. Spec still changes reflections and the visible impression.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, hood.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Confirm the selected zone/layer and exact finish ID.
For primary-base material changes on an existing livery, choose BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only).
Choose Use finish’s own color when the generated palette is part of the intended design.
Check patterns, additional bases and HSB adjustments separately before claiming the composed paint is unchanged.
tips: Source mode can use a colour-generating primary base for its spec without running its paint palette.
Colour-bearing finish mode is useful when its palette belongs in the intended design.
pitfalls: Do not confuse the registered paint function with the BASE COLOR mode actually executing it.
Do not extend primary-base source-lock proof to the entire composed document.
A static interference palette is not proof of dynamic camera-angle colour flipping.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 145 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 56 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal varies by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Colour-generating construction is not the same as executing that paint pass: Use source paint bypasses the reviewed ordinary primary base paint function.

This is one of the five colour-bearing Foundation exceptions, not a plain source-passing material. Registered M/R/CC seed values are not uniform output values or a tested recommendation for your car. Source inspection describes construction; final appearance and any angle-dependent claim require actual in-sim inspection. In the reviewed ordinary primary-base compositor, BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only) skips the primary base paint function, including a colour-generating one. Use finish’s own color allows that palette to run. This preserves the source from the primary base paint pass, not from every other operation: patterns, additional bases, hue/saturation/brightness, explicit colour overrides and target/mask choices need separate checks. Spec still changes reflections and the visible impression.

faq.q: Can I use chameleon spec without adding its paint colours?
faq.a: Yes for the reviewed ordinary primary-base path: choose BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only), which skips that base paint function while retaining its material contribution. This is not a whole-project colour guarantee; patterns, additional bases and HSB need separate checks.

faq.q: Does Foundation chameleon leave sponsor colours unchanged?
faq.a: It depends on BASE COLOR mode. Use source paint (spec only) skips the reviewed ordinary primary base paint function, so this primary base does not add its palette. Use finish’s own color runs its paint construction. Other operations can still change the livery; inspect patterns, additional bases, HSB and the target.

faq.q: Are Orchid Shift Pearl material numbers constant everywhere?
faq.a: No. Its registered spec function varies metal and roughness spatially; clearcoat starts at 16. Catalog averages and registry seed values are not constant output values.

faq.q: Does Orchid Shift Pearl automatically change colour with camera angle?
faq.a: The generated paint uses static spatial colour fields; the source functions accept no live camera angle. Actual lighting and reflection can affect appearance, but an angle-changing pigment effect must be checked in iRacing rather than promised from the name.

articles.title: Eggshell
articles.summary: Smooth eggshell finish in the selected colour, with a faint soft sheen; verify the noisy legacy thumbnail separately before teaching grain as a feature. Your colour with a very soft diffuse sheen, just above fully matte; no texture, no sparkle.
articles.what: Eggshell is a plain Foundation material starting at M/R/CC 0/140/100. Its own paint function adds no pattern, and its base spec is constant: it does not draw grain, flakes or brush marks. Choose BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only) to preserve the source artwork rather than replace its colours with a solid colour. Metallic response, roughness, clearcoat, lighting and reflections still change the visible impression. Other layers, patterns, masks and zone adjustments can change the composed spec, so these starting values are not a promise for every exported pixel.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the Base Material box under BASE (it shows the zone's current base, or "Click to choose a base" on an empty zone) and type "Eggshell" in the search box at the top of the picker.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
To keep existing artwork, choose BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only). Choose Use solid color only when you intend to replace its colour.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole car: uniform finish
Hood and roof where glare would bother
Neutral and clean: numbers in any colour read with full contrast.
Any graphics: stripes, numbers, flames print cleanly over a plain base
Pairs well with: gloss black, chrome, any colour you give it, white.
pitfalls: Not matte: it has a faint sheen (roughness 140, less rough than matte at 215)
Not satin: satin is glossier, this is a step duller
Avoid: expecting grain or texture, very bright colours can look flat.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 0 (non-metal paint), roughness 140 (semi-matte), clearcoat 100 (moderate clearcoat, satin range). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: A semi-matte surface mutes the paint colour a little, so a clean saturated colour looks best; pair it with a gloss or metal neighbour for contrast. Avoid: expecting grain or texture, very bright colours can look flat.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any graphics: stripes, numbers, flames print cleanly over a plain base; carbon or camo patterns: the base adds no competing noise
Patterns to avoid: glitter or flake overlays: sparkle on an eggshell sheen looks wrong; chrome or mirror graphics: wrong finish family
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear logos or stripes: shiny accents on a soft body; fine grain spec: a hint of tooth
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

examples.title: Preserve artwork while changing material
examples.goal: Try Eggshell without replacing the source paint.
examples.result: Source paint is retained by this plain material; reflections and material response change its lit appearance. Check the composed spec and protect sponsor/number material separately.

faq.q: What are the starting spec values for Eggshell?
faq.a: The registered plain Foundation material starts at M/R/CC 0/140/100. The base spec is constant, not a grain or flake texture. Patterns, blends, masks and adjustments may change the composed result.

faq.q: Can I keep my existing paint colours with Eggshell?
faq.a: Use BASE COLOR Use source paint (spec only) rather than Use solid color. This plain base preserves the source paint pixels, but metallic response, reflections and lighting still change their appearance. Source-colour preservation does not automatically protect sponsor and number material.
